title: Well-ordered sets: least elements, induction, and recursion

based_on.title: Set Theory
based_on.pages: 29–31 (section 6, especially Lemma 6.2 and Theorem 6.6), notes updated January 31, 2026

summary: Study well-orders and their initial segments, prove induction from least counterexamples, and construct unique recursive functions from rules on earlier histories.
abstract: A well-order guarantees a first element in every nonempty selection, even though a point may have infinitely many elements before it. This extends the familiar ideas of induction and recursion beyond the natural numbers. A property holds throughout the order if, at each point, its truth at all earlier points implies its truth there. Likewise, rules that assign exactly one value for every possible earlier history determine a unique function, including at points with no last earlier element.
